questions.stem: The number of terms in the series \(\displaystyle\sum_{r=28}^{57}(2r+1)\) is:
questions.hint: The number of integers from 28 to 57 inclusive is \(57-28+1\).

steps.explain: The number of terms in a sum from \(r=a\) to \(r=b\) inclusive is \(b-a+1\).

questions.stem: (e) A sequence is defined by \(t_1=3\) and \(t_{n+1}=\dfrac{1+3t_n}{3+t_n}\) for all integers \(n\ge1\). Evaluate \(t_3\).
questions.hint: Find \(t_2\) first using the recursive formula with \(t_1=3\), then use \(t_2\) to find \(t_3\).

steps.explain: Substitute \(t_1=3\) into the recursive formula to find \(t_2\).
Substitute \(t_2=\tfrac53\) into the formula to find \(t_3\).
Simplify by multiplying by the reciprocal.

questions.stem: Bottles are packed into a box with a piece of packing between each pair of neighbouring bottles, as shown (\(n=4\), \(k=3\)). How many pieces of packing are needed to pack a rectangular box fully, if the box has \(n\) bottles along the length and \(k\) bottles across the breadth?
questions.hint: Count the pieces between side-by-side bottles and the pieces between front-and-back bottles separately.

steps.explain: Each row of \(n\) bottles has \(n-1\) gaps, and there are \(k\) rows.
Each column of \(k\) bottles has \(k-1\) gaps, and there are \(n\) columns.
Add both kinds and check against the diagram (\(9+8=17\) pieces).

questions.stem: (c)(i) Find the values of \(y\) so that the quadratic equation \(x^2+(y-1)x+y=0\) has real roots. (ii) Hence, or otherwise, find the range of the function \(y=\dfrac{x-x^2}{x+1}\), to 1 decimal place. (iii) Find the oblique asymptote for the graph of \(y=\dfrac{x-x^2}{x+1}\). (iv) Sketch the graph of \(y=\dfrac{x-x^2}{x+1}\) for \(-3\le x\le4\), labelling all intercepts and asymptotes.

steps.explain: Real roots require a non-negative discriminant: \(\Delta=(y-1)^2-4(1)(y)\ge0\).
Solve the corresponding equality \(y^2-6y+1=0\) using the quadratic formula.
Since this upward parabola in \(y\) is \(\ge0\) outside its roots, state the solution set.

For part (ii): rearranging \(y=\dfrac{x-x^2}{x+1}\) as \(y(x+1)=x-x^2 \Rightarrow x^2+(y-1)x+y=0\) shows this is EXACTLY the equation from part (i) — so the range of the function is precisely the set of \(y\)-values for which this equation has a real solution for \(x\).
Evaluate the boundary values numerically, to 1 decimal place.
For part (iii): perform polynomial long division on \(\dfrac{-x^2+x}{x+1}\) to find the oblique asymptote (the quotient term, ignoring the remainder).
As \(x\to\pm\infty\), the remainder term vanishes, leaving the oblique asymptote.

For part (iv): the curve has a vertical asymptote at \(x=-1\) (where the denominator is zero) and the oblique asymptote \(y=-x+2\) found above. \(x\)-intercepts are at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) (where \(x-x^2=0\)); \(y\)-intercept is also \(0\) (at \(x=0\)). Sketch both branches as shown above.
steps.work: Vertical asymptote \(x=-1\); oblique asymptote \(y=-x+2\); intercepts at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).

questions.stem: Four identical circles of radius r are drawn inside a square, as shown in the diagram below. The region enclosed by the circles has been shaded in the diagram. The shaded area can be found using:

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="360" height="220" viewBox="0 0 360 220"><rect width="360" height="220" fill="#fff"/><rect x="60" y="25" width="160" height="160" fill="#fff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="100" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><path d="M140 65 C140 87 158 105 180 105 C158 105 140 123 140 145 C140 123 122 105 100 105 C122 105 140 87 140 65Z" fill="#10b981" fill-opacity=".78" stroke="#047857" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="100" y1="65" x2="140" y2="65" stroke="#047857" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="2.2" fill="#047857"/><rect x="112" y="49" width="17" height="14" rx="3" fill="#ffffff" fill-opacity=".92"/><text x="117" y="60" font-size="12" fill="#047857" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-weight="700">r</text></svg>

questions.hint: r is the radius: the distance from a circle’s centre to its circumference. The central square has side 2r, and its four corner pieces are four quarter-circles of radius r.

steps.explain: The marked segment r runs from a circle’s centre to its circumference, so it is a radius. The four circle centres form a square, and adjacent centres are one diameter apart: 2r.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="360" height="220" viewBox="0 0 360 220"><rect width="360" height="220" fill="#fff"/><rect x="60" y="25" width="160" height="160" fill="#fff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="100" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><rect x="100" y="65" width="80" height="80" fill="#fbbf24" fill-opacity=".20" stroke="#f97316" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="100" y1="65" x2="140" y2="65" stroke="#047857" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="2.2" fill="#047857"/><rect x="112" y="49" width="17" height="14" rx="3" fill="#ffffff" fill-opacity=".92"/><text x="117" y="60" font-size="12" fill="#047857" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-weight="700">r</text><text x="242" y="113" font-size="12" fill="#9a3412" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-weight="600">Square side = 2r</text></svg>

steps.explain: Inside this square, the four curved pieces are four quarter-circles. Together they have the area of one complete circle of radius r.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="360" height="220" viewBox="0 0 360 220"><rect width="360" height="220" fill="#fff"/><rect x="60" y="25" width="160" height="160" fill="#fff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="65" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="100" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><circle cx="180" cy="145" r="40" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><defs><clipPath id="inner"><rect x="100" y="65" width="80" height="80"/></clipPath></defs><g clip-path="url(#inner)" fill="#fbbf24" fill-opacity=".65" stroke="#f97316" stroke-width="1.3"><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="40"/><circle cx="180" cy="65" r="40"/><circle cx="100" cy="145" r="40"/><circle cx="180" cy="145" r="40"/></g><line x1="100" y1="65" x2="140" y2="65" stroke="#047857" stroke-width="2.2" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="100" cy="65" r="2.2" fill="#047857"/><rect x="112" y="49" width="17" height="14" rx="3" fill="#ffffff" fill-opacity=".92"/><text x="117" y="60" font-size="12" fill="#047857" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-weight="700">r</text><text x="242" y="113" font-size="12" fill="#9a3412" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-weight="600">4 quarters = 1 circle</text></svg>

steps.explain: Subtract the four quarter-circles from the inner square. This gives the shaded area and matches option B.

keyPoints.text: The region enclosed by the circles
keyPoints.note: Subtract the four quarter-circles (one full circle total) from the central square of side 2r.
